strengths: Complete human-subjects documentation: three ethics reviews including an ethics working group with a published memorandum, four consent modes with re-consent and withdrawal terms, exact compensation, at-risk protections and Safe Harbor de-identification with an honest residual-risk statement.

Persistent identification and sustainability: PhysioNet DOIs per version plus a concept DOI, RRID, six dated releases across two platforms, errata changelog, semi-annual cadence, named maintainers and retention terms.

Two-tier access model (registered features on PhysioNet, controlled raw audio via Synapse and the DACO) documented end to end with license, agreements, IP terms, governance office and contact address.

Preprocessing is parameterised for replication (16 kHz mono with Butterworth filter, STFT 25 ms/10 ms/400-point, 60 Mel bins, sparc 50 Hz, ppgs 100 Hz) with named open-source repositories and licenses.

Disciplined source handling: an explicit referent statement, recording-count and enrollment-target conflicts resolved with declared source preferences, the pediatric dataset typed as is_supplemented_by and the HDN v1.0 release as is_new_version_of.
weaknesses: Only four generic keywords, limiting discoverability.
No resources or file_collections enumeration; per-file counts survive only in source_caveats prose, and no demographic distributions or per-cohort counts are given.
data_protection_impacts absent entirely, without even the sibling record's declaration that no impact analysis was conducted.
Release collection window undated ('12 months') and explicitly unreconciled with the four-year protocol timeline.
